headline: Molecules are atoms bonded together—and those bonds are where chemistry happens
universal_truth: Connection transforms; what's bonded becomes more than the sum of its parts
fun_facts: A water molecule has two hydrogen atoms bonded to one oxygen—that simple bond creates oceans
Your body contains millions of different types of molecules, from simple to incredibly complex
DNA molecules are so long that if unwound, the DNA in one cell would stretch 6 feet
discussion_questions: How does connection transform things—making the whole greater than the parts?
What bonds in your life have created something new that didn't exist before?
What's the difference between a mere collection and a bonded combination?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Atoms alone are building blocks. But atoms bonded together—that's where magic happens. Water, DNA, proteins, plastics, medicines—all molecules, all atoms connected in specific ways. The bonds between atoms are where chemistry creates reality.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Why do atoms bond? They don't just stick together randomly. Some combinations form eagerly; others never bond at all. What makes atoms want to connect, and what determines who bonds with whom?

options.text: Atoms bond to achieve stable electron configurations—sharing or transferring electrons
options.response: Yes. Atoms seek stability through their electrons. Bonding completes them.

options.text: Atoms are attracted by gravity and stick together when close

q1.title: Seeking Stability
q1.script: Atoms bond because they're seeking stability. Most atoms have incomplete outer electron shells. By sharing electrons with other atoms, they achieve stable configurations. Bonding completes them. Chemistry is atoms finding stability through connection.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Seeking Stability"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: New Properties Emerge
q2.script: Sodium is a reactive metal. Chlorine is a toxic gas. Bond them together and you get table salt—essential for life. The molecule has entirely different properties than its components. Connection creates transformation.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Complexity From Simplicity
q3.script: DNA is just four types of molecular units repeated billions of times. Yet those simple units, bonded in sequence, encode all the instructions to build a human. Simple connections, repeated and arranged, create unlimited complexity.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Connection transforms. Atoms teach us that bonding creates properties that didn't exist before—not just addition, but transformation. Your connections don't just add to you; they change what you can become.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 77. Tomorrow, we'll explore the tiny units of life—cells. Until then, appreciate the molecular bonds that make your body, your world, and your thoughts possible.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Transformative Bonds - Connect to Become More
growTrack.learning_objective: Seek connections that transform, not just add
growTrack.activity: Think of a connection that transformed you—a relationship, community, or experience that didn't just add to your life but changed what you could become. What made it transformative? How can you cultivate more bonds like that?
